material_finding: The donor voice task bridge and the Triggerword-4 native-subagent contract cover two distinct runtime actor classes that must not be silently collapsed: realtime voice delegates through a fresh/resumed headless `claude -p` process/session, while the newer R2 design also targets native subagent actors. A native SubagentStart/SubagentStop proof does not automatically prove attribution/policy/effect lineage for the headless voice child path.

atoms.what_it_does: RealtimeSession._claude_taetigkeit calls gespraechsmodus.claude_frage with the stored Claude session id and mutable berechtigung, then persists a returned session id. It passes no cwd, workpackage_id, agent_id, task_id or tool invocation identity.

claude_frage directly constructs and executes `claude -p` with JSON output, permission mode, hard Bash denial and append-system-prompt. It creates a new session with --session-id or resumes one with --resume; subprocess cwd falls back to Path.home(). The donor code does not invoke a parent Agent/subagent spawn primitive in this path.

The versioned donor plugin routes seven hook event classes through stern.py: SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit, PreToolUse, PostToolUse, Stop, SessionEnd and PreCompact. Dedicated SubagentStart/SubagentStop/Task lifecycle registration is absent in this file.

architecture_delta.work_execution_binding_addition: Bind execution_actor_class plus spawn/invocation mechanism. Do not infer native-subagent lifecycle evidence for a headless `claude -p` session child.
architecture_delta.child_policy_envelope_addition: Bind policy evidence separately for each actor class because loaded settings/hooks/cwd/tool surfaces can differ between direct headless CLI sessions and native subagent execution.
architecture_delta.effect_lineage_addition: Each mutating call still requires exact invocation identity and deterministic pre-side-effect enforcement regardless of actor class.
architecture_delta.completion_addition: Completion credit must bind terminal evidence from the same actor class and generation that executed the work. Session resume continuity is not by itself child-actor identity proof.

contradictions.a: Triggerword-4 R2 now specifies native child actor/task/invocation binding and SubagentStart/equivalent lifecycle evidence.
contradictions.b: The current donor voice task path directly launches/resumes `claude -p` and does not source-prove a native subagent spawn relation.

counterhypotheses.claim: The installed Claude Code runtime may emit enough equivalent lifecycle/tool identity for direct headless `claude -p` sessions that both classes can share one implementation after measurement.
counterhypotheses.discriminator: Run one harmless HEADLESS_SESSION_CHILD probe and one harmless NATIVE_SUBAGENT_CHILD probe on an authorized host; compare actual lifecycle event sets, actor/task IDs, loaded policy provenance, cwd/isolation semantics and per-tool invocation identity.

counterhypotheses.claim: The voice path may later be migrated entirely onto native subagents, making the headless class compatibility-only.
counterhypotheses.discriminator: Do not retire headless support until the installed native path reproduces session continuity, policy containment, latency and result re-entry requirements with executable receipts.

trigger4_feed.rule: NATIVE_SUBAGENT_RUNTIME_PASS does not imply HEADLESS_SESSION_CHILD_RUNTIME_PASS. Voice/delegated-task acceptance must either prove both actor classes actually used by 2.0 or explicitly retire one with executable migration evidence.
trigger4_feed.highest_value_next_test: Paired harmless actor-class probe: same bounded work intent through direct headless `claude -p` and native subagent path; capture exact build/settings/hooks/cwd/actor/task/tool identity and terminal result for differential comparison.
